paras: The killing of Jack Hendricks was the fatal shooting of a Black man by Constable Wright in Campbell County, Virginia, near Lynchburg, on November 9, 1882. Hendricks was under arrest for "malicious cutting," and the only published account, a brief Lynchburg dispatch, said he was shot while trying to escape. The dispatch ran the next day in papers from Richmond to Dallas and St. Paul, usually as a single line among other news.

According to the Lynchburg dispatch dated November 9, Constable Wright "to-day shot and killed a negro named Jack Hendricks," who had been arrested on a charge of malicious cutting. The dispatch said Hendricks "tried to escape from an officer while under arrest" and placed the shooting in Campbell County, near Lynchburg. It gave no hour, exact spot, or name of the person Hendricks was accused of cutting, and the escape attempt is reported only as the officer's side of the event.
No report of an inquest, an inquiry into the constable's conduct, or any later mention of the case appears in the coverage.

Every version traced to the same short Lynchburg telegram, which the Knoxville Daily Chronicle printed in full a day later, and none added detail beyond it. The Richmond Daily Dispatch headed the item "Negro Killed by an Officer," while the Dallas Daily Herald ran it under "Sonegambian Shot" and printed the victim's name as "Jake Hendricks." The Washington Evening Critic, which called Hendricks "a colored man," and the Alexandria Gazette included the item in columns of news notes, and the Savannah Morning News and the St. Paul Daily Globe carried shortened versions, the Globe's reading only that Wright "shot dead Jack Hendricks, a negro, who tried to escape." All of these papers repeated the escape claim as fact and without comment, and no Black-press coverage of the case was found.

reader.title: Killing of Jack Hendricks
bases: Every report says a constable, Wright, shot and killed Hendricks while he was under arrest; no crowd or mob appears (A1, A2, A3).
All versions are copies of one Lynchburg dispatch of November 9 giving the officer's side; no independent local account, inquest or follow-up was found (A1, A2, A3).

framing.detail: The Richmond Dispatch headed the item 'Negro Killed by an Officer' and repeated the escape claim without comment.
The Dallas Daily Herald headed the same dispatch 'Sonegambian Shot.'
Washington, Alexandria, St. Paul and Savannah papers ran it as a one- or two-line item in news-summary columns.

conflicts.note: Most copies of the dispatch print 'Jack'; 'Jake' appears only in the Dallas Herald and is likely a copying variant.
